items.stem: Define the term 'motivation'.
items.answer: The factors that make a person work willingly and well to achieve goals.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The factors that make a person work willingly and well to achieve goals. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between hygiene factors and motivators in Herzberg's theory.
items.answer: Hygiene factors such as pay and conditions prevent dissatisfaction if they are good enough but do not motivate; motivators such as recognition and responsibility come from the job itself and create satisfaction and motivation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark hygiene factors; 1 mark motivators; 1 mark contrast with examples. [3]

items.stem: Explain one limitation of Maslow's hierarchy of needs for managers.
items.answer: People do not always satisfy needs in the same order and it is hard to know which level each employee is at, so it is difficult to use in practice.
items.markingKey: 1 mark limitation; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Savanna Fresh Ltd is a private limited company based in Nairobi, Kenya. It grows cut flowers and green beans and exports them by air to supermarkets in Europe and employs about 850 people. Its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use. Explain how Herzberg's two-factor theory could help managers at Savanna Fresh improve motivation.
items.answer: Points to develop for Savanna Fresh: hygiene factors and motivators; improve hygiene factors to remove dissatisfaction; job enrichment and recognition to motivate; motivated staff raise productivity.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: hygiene factors and motivators. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Savanna Fresh (horticulture). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. improve hygiene factors to remove dissatisfaction; job enrichment and recognition to motivate. [3]

items.stem: Andina Solar is a private limited company in Santiago, Chile with about 380 staff. It designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes. The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Explain how Andina Solar could use Maslow's hierarchy of needs to motivate its employees.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andina Solar: Maslow's five levels of needs; fair pay and safe conditions meet lower needs; teamwork meets social needs; recognition and promotion meet esteem and self-actualisation needs.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: Maslow's five levels of needs. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Andina Solar (renewable energy). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. fair pay and safe conditions meet lower needs; teamwork meets social needs. [3]

items.stem: Explain how a manager could use McClelland's theory to motivate employees.
items.answer: Give employees with a high need for achievement challenging tasks and feedback, those with a need for affiliation teamwork, and those with a need for power leadership roles.
items.markingKey: 1 mark identify the need; 1 mark matching job design; 1 mark second need applied. [3]

items.stem: Define the term 'scientific management'.
items.answer: Taylor's approach of studying tasks to find the most efficient method, training workers in it and paying them by results.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Taylor's approach of studying tasks to find the most efficient method, training workers in it and paying them by results. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the main features of Taylor's scientific management.
items.answer: Tasks are studied (time and motion) to find the most efficient method, workers are trained to follow it and are paid by results such as piece rates, with close supervision.
items.markingKey: 1 mark time and motion/best method; 1 mark training/supervision; 1 mark pay by results. [3]

items.stem: Explain the three elements of Vroom's expectancy theory.
items.answer: Expectancy: effort will lead to better performance; instrumentality: performance will be rewarded; valence: the employee values the reward. Motivation is high only if all three are strong.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for expectancy, instrumentality and valence. [3]

items.stem: The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Andes Textil SA, a family-owned private company in Peru with about 320 employees, makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan. Explain the likely effects of introducing scientific management at Andes Textil.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andes Textil: Taylor studied tasks to find the most efficient method; productivity rises in routine tasks; workers may become demotivated by repetitive work; labour relations may suffer.

items.stem: Define the term 'commission'.
items.answer: A payment to a salesperson based on a percentage of the value of sales they make.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A payment to a salesperson based on a percentage of the value of sales they make. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of paying production workers a piece rate.
items.answer: Advantage: it encourages higher output because pay rises with production. Disadvantage: workers may rush, reducing quality, and income is uncertain if machines break down.
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage, 1 mark explanation; 1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation. [4]

items.stem: Explain why financial rewards may not motivate all employees.
items.answer: According to Herzberg pay is a hygiene factor: once pay is fair, extra money may not motivate, and many employees value recognition, responsibility or security more.
items.markingKey: 1 mark Herzberg/hygiene; 1 mark other needs valued. [2]

items.answer: Points to develop for Tejo Mobility: financial methods include piece rate, commission, bonus and profit sharing; pay linked to output or sales encourages effort; bonuses for targets focus effort; profit sharing builds identity with the business.

items.stem: Define the term 'job enrichment'.
items.answer: Redesigning a job to give the employee more responsibility, a complete unit of work and more challenging tasks.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Redesigning a job to give the employee more responsibility, a complete unit of work and more challenging tasks. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between job enrichment and job rotation.
items.answer: Job enrichment gives the employee more responsibility and more challenging work; job rotation moves the employee between tasks at the same level, giving variety but not more responsibility.
items.markingKey: 1 mark enrichment; 1 mark rotation; 1 mark contrast (responsibility). [3]

items.stem: Explain two benefits of teamworking for a business.
items.answer: Employees share skills and ideas, improving problem solving and quality; and working in a team meets social needs, raising motivation and reducing absence.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark benefit, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'motivation'?

The factors that make a person work willingly and well to achieve goals.
In Herzberg's theory, factors such as achievement, recognition, responsibility and the work itself that lead to job satisfaction and motivation.
Giving employees the authority and resources to make decisions about their own work.
